scientific_question: Does persistently learning a causal common prerequisite P unlock positive subsequent learning gain across multiple previously stalled target families T?
core_contrast: Second-stage change from learning T after learning P versus learning T after an equally costly non-prerequisite control C; baseline direct transfer before stage T must be subtracted.
unit_of_analysis: independent prerequisite family × downstream target family × model initialization seed

second_stage.prompt: remove all prerequisite scaffolds and lesson traces
second_stage.measurement: unseen T performance before and after second-stage update

strongest_collision_boundary: SkillGraph/SkillDAG/SE-GoS already build and evolve skill graphs; SOAR already uses real learning gains for bridge curricula. Main novelty requires causal stage-2 task trainability gains after persistent update, not retrieval accuracy or first-stage improvement.
stats: pair seeds and task family; cluster confidence intervals by family/seed and disclose all negative controls
go: causal prerequisite × dependent-task effect stable beyond matched high-frequency non-prerequisite, direct practice, and bridge curriculum; blind discovery under budget; later multi-round gains
merge: only direct error transfer (I8) or curriculum ordering effect (I9), no stage-two learning interaction
stop: hubs and unrelated prerequisites work equally, or effect disappears after total-budget and leakage controls
